_comment: EXAMPLE / TEMPLATE — copy to .guardrails/release-artifact-contract.json to
enable the ARTIFACT VERIFY stage in scripts/deploy.sh. When the real file is
absent the stage prints a skip notice and the deploy continues, so a fresh
DevGate install needs no configuration.
The stage packs your project with its own package manager, lists the archive,
and asserts every 'must_contain' entry is REALLY inside it before publishing.
A published version is immutable: a package manager will happily produce a
well-formed archive with the built binary missing, and the failure only shows
up at install time for every user.
Fields:
artifact_glob      — glob for the packed artifact, relative to the project
root. Matched after packing (e.g. 'my-tool-*.tgz',
'dist/*.whl', 'target/package/*.crate').
must_contain       — archive entries that MUST be present, exact match.
Do NOT include the archive's own top-level prefix; set
'entry_prefix' instead so the same list works across
package managers.
must_be_executable — paths relative to the project root whose on-disk
executable bit is checked (a non-executable launcher
breaks the installer's spawn).
entry_prefix       — prefix the packer adds to every archive entry. npm
uses 'package/'; cargo uses '<name>-<version>/'; set
"" when the packer adds none.
